citations.narrative:
Two bags of feed were being stored in an area with numerous tools, chemicals and various maintenance equipment.
Housing facilities must be kept neat and free of clutter, including equipment, furniture, and stored material, but may
contain materials actually used and necessary for cleaning the area, and fixtures or equipment necessary for proper
husbandry practices or research needs.
To be corrected from the date of inspection, 9-3-2026, forward.

Two bags of open bird feed were stored on the floor. A second building had an open container of food stored on the floor
that was uncovered and was contaminated with numerous rodent droppings. Rodent waste may contain disease causing
organisms which could cause harm to the birds.
Supplies of food, including food supplements, bedding, and substrate must be stored in a manner that protects the
supplies from deterioration, spoilage (harmful microbial growth), contamination, and vermin infestation. The supplies must
be stored off the floor and away from the walls, to allow cleaning underneath and around the supplies.
To be corrected by 9-5-2026.

citations.desc: Primary enclosures used to transport live birds.
citations.narrative:
None of the primary enclosures being used to transport several birds were marked with the words “Live Animals”. Correct
marking of enclosures helps to ensure the birds are not subjected to handling which could cause injury during shipment.
Unless the enclosure is permanently affixed to the conveyance, it is clearly marked on top and on one or more sides with
the words “Live Animals,” in letters at least 1 inch (2.5 centimeters) high, and with arrows or other markings to indicate the
correct upright position of the primary enclosure.
To be corrected prior to the next transport.

A shipment of birds was received the evening prior to the inspection, and the birds were being held more than 12 hours
without access to water. Water deprivation may lead to dehydration and disease conditions that may cause serious health
problems to birds.
Dealers, exhibitors, research facilities, and operators of auction sales must provide potable water to all weaned birds
transported in their own primary conveyance at least every 12 hours after such transportation is initiated, except for birds
which, according to professionally accepted standards or under the direction of the attending veterinarian, require
watering or feeding more or less frequently.
To be corrected from the date of inspection, 9-3-2026, forward.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with a facility representative.
Additional Inspectors:
WILLIAM SNOW n
